steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Science fiction is a genre that explores imagined futures, alternative realities and the consequences of scientific and technological advancement.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Core sci-fi themes include the relationship between humanity and technology, encounters with the alien or other, dystopian societies and the limits of knowledge.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sci-fi iconography includes spaceships, futuristic cityscapes, advanced technology interfaces, alien creatures, robots and space suits.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sci-fi settings range from deep space and alien planets to near-future Earth, dystopian cities and virtual reality environments.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always connect sci-fi's speculative elements to the real-world concerns they reflect — examiners want to see this link made explicit. Use specific iconographic examples from your set films rather than discussing sci-fi iconography in general. Identify which sub-genre your film belongs to and explain how it uses or subverts that sub-genre's conventions. Consider the historical context of your film's production — what anxieties were current when it was made? Discuss how sci-fi's visual design — special effects, production design, cinematography — contributes to its meaning.
